findings.issue: Still open from round 1, because tools/ci/retry.js did not change in f4a6897. The root-level `sudo -n kill -- -<pgid>` can fire without a fresh groupExists check. If the group has emptied and its pgid has been reused, the root kill could hit an unrelated process group.
findings.evidence: pgid comes from child.pid, which is trusted -> killGroup gets EPERM -> sudoKillGroup runs as root. There is no attacker-controlled input. The pid would have to be recycled within a window of milliseconds to about 2 s on an ephemeral runner, so there is no reachable exploit.
findings.fix: Optional: in stopGroup, call groupExists(pid) right before sudoKill and skip the sudo call on ESRCH.

findings.issue: Still open from round 1, because the cleanUp code did not change. The `sudo -n pkill -KILL -f` pattern is an unanchored substring of a random 9-digit marker.
findings.evidence: The marker comes from crypto.randomInt and is passed as an argv element with no shell. A collision is practically impossible.
findings.fix: Optional: anchor the pattern to the expected argv tail.

findings.issue: The new processLayout() diagnostic puts the full args of every process whose command line contains 'sudo' into the assertion message. On a failure, that text lands in the CI log. If another job step ever passes a secret on a sudo command line at the same moment, the secret would be printed.
findings.evidence: ps -eo ...,args comes from local process state, not untrusted input. The output appears only when an assertion fails, in a test that runs only on Linux CI. The runner is ephemeral, nothing else runs in parallel during vitest, and GitHub Actions masks registered secrets. No secret reaches this path today.
findings.fix: Optional: filter only on the marker, or on sudo lines whose pgid/sid match the helper's child, instead of on every line containing 'sudo'.

summary: In round 2 the fix commit f4a6897 changes only tests/ci/retry.sudo.test.ts. It adds stronger assertions and a `ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid,sid,user,args` diagnostic that is called through spawnSync with a fixed argv and no shell. The marker is used only for in-process string filtering. No new privileged operation, injection path or dependency was added. Round 1 had no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Its MINOR (pgid reuse before the root kill) and NIT (unanchored pkill) stay open because that code did not change. One new NIT: the diagnostic prints the args of all sudo processes into failure messages. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
